# UI test fixtures

Everything in this directory is test data for `ui/tests/*.spec.js`, which runs under
`node --test` from `scripts/check-ui-behaviour.sh` on every `just lint`. The `*.json` files are
shaped like objects the Kubernetes API server returns, field for field from the CRD types in
`crates/weirkeeper/src/crds/`; where an object references a Secret, only its **name** is present,
because a name is not a secret and nothing in this product renders a credential.

## The throwaway keypair

`approver.pem` and `approver.pub.pem` are a **throwaway test fixture**, checked in on the precedent
of [`e2e/fixtures/signed/signing.pem`](../../../e2e/fixtures/signed/README.md), whose README states
the rule this one repeats: **the P-256 key pair here signs nothing outside this repository's own
test suite and must never be used to sign a real drill scorecard.** It is unencrypted PKCS#8, it
authorises nothing, it appears in no `TrustRoster` any cluster loads, and rotating it costs nothing
but a re-run of the test that uses it.

It exists because one assertion cannot be made without a real invocation:
`the_plan_hash_the_page_shows_is_the_hash_the_cli_computes` spawns the release `logweir` binary,
because `logweir drill approve` requires `--key`, and compares the `plan_hash` line it prints with
`await planHash(bytes)` computed in the browser's own `crypto.subtle`. The value of that test is
that the two numbers come from two languages; a stub would make it a test of one.

It was generated in this worktree with the two commands `scripts/demo.sh` uses:

```
openssl ecparam -genkey -name prime256v1 -noout | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -out approver.pem
openssl ec -in approver.pem -pubout -out approver.pub.pem
```

Its fingerprint -- the same digest `logweir` uses as a key id, and the one the keys page prints the
command for -- is `24f4f5a02694bdf2e800a471545287d2c5d4b4b361212bb270ab4a4722921cdd`.

**No other private key is checked in anywhere by this task, and no page in this product accepts,
uploads, proxies or generates one** (Global Constraint 28).

## The plan golden

`plan-fields.json` is the wizard state `renderPlanBytes` is called with; `plan.golden.yaml` is what
it renders. The two arms of `render_plan_bytes_emits_a_document_the_runner_parses` are what make the
golden mean something:

- **arm 1**, in `crates/logweir/tests/ui_lint.rs`, deserialises the golden into
  `logweir_core::spec::RestoreSpec` -- the runner's own type -- and compares `target.mode`,
  `target.topic_naming.prefix` and `restore.point_in_time` with `plan-fields.json`;
- **arm 2**, in `pages.spec.js`, byte-compares `renderPlanBytes(plan-fields.json)` with the
  committed golden, length included.

Regenerate it with:

```
node ui/tests/emit-plan.js > ui/tests/fixtures/plan.golden.yaml
```

`scripts/check-ui-behaviour.sh` runs that emitter into a temporary file and `diff -u`s it against
the committed bytes on every lint, so a regenerated golden and the committed one cannot drift.
Regenerating it is not the same as making it correct: arm 1 reads the regenerated bytes from Rust,
so a golden regenerated from an emitter that invented a shape fails there even once the two
JavaScript halves agree with each other.
